title: Vault Tumblers
summary: Crack vaults whose clue plates are linear equations: find the code with the inverse A⁻¹ = adj A / |A|, and spot the jammed ones.
subject: mathematics
ncertRef: Section 4.6, Applications of determinants and matrices
concepts: Adjoint and inverse of a matrix
Solving AX = B by X = A⁻¹B
learningOutcome: The student can find the determinant and adjoint, solve AX = B with the inverse, and tell from |A| and (adj A)B whether a system has one, no, or many solutions.

levels.title: Two plates
levels.adds: Baseline: write two equations as AX = B and solve with X = A⁻¹B, using |A| = ad − bc and adj A = [d −b; −c a] (Ex 4.4 Q1, Q5; Ex 4.5 Q7 to Q10).
hints: Write the plates as a matrix A and a column B.
|A| = ad − bc. If it is not zero, A⁻¹ = adj A / |A|.
Swap the diagonal of A, negate the other two entries to get adj A, then multiply by B.

levels.title: Three plates
levels.adds: Harder: 3 by 3 systems: expand |A| along a row, build the cofactors, take the transpose to get adj A (Ex 4.4 Q7 to Q11; Ex 4.5 Q11 to Q14).
hints: Expand |A| along a row, with the signs + − + from the checkerboard.
Each cofactor is (−1)^(i+j) times a 2 by 2 minor.
adj A is the transpose of the cofactor matrix; X = (adj A)B / |A|.

levels.title: Shopping bills
levels.adds: New: a word problem becomes AX = B, with the prices as the unknowns (Ex 4.5 Q16; Example 18).
hints: Each bill is one equation: units of each good times its price.
The coefficients are the quantities in each shopper’s basket.
Then solve AX = B as before.

levels.title: The jammed vault
levels.adds: New: when |A| = 0 there is no inverse; (adj A)B = O means many solutions, otherwise none (Ex 4.5 Q1 to Q6).
hints: Find |A| first. A non-zero value means exactly one code.
If |A| = 0, look at the plates: can one be made from the others?
(adj A)B = O means consistent with many codes; (adj A)B ≠ O means no code.

misconceptions: Every system of equations has exactly one solution
A matrix with |A| = 0 has an inverse
The adjoint is just the transpose of A
